simple.meaning: רָזַם (râzam) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to twinkle the eye (in mockery).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Job, beginning at Job 15:12. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָזַם (H7335) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: רָזַם (râzam) / H7335 is traced through Job 15:12 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H7335. razam [ רָזַם ] verb wink, flash (of eyes) (transposed [textual error ?] for Arabic , Aramaic רְמַז , ; so Late Hebrew רָמַז (rare), רֶמֶז sign, intimation ); — Qal Imperfect 3masculine plural עֵינֶיךָ וּמַהיִּֿרְזְמוּן Job 15:12 (Manuscripts ירמזון ) why do thine eyes flash (in wrath)? but possibly read יְרוּמוּן ( Prov 6:17 ; 30:13 , etc., compare Bu).
